name: Psych behind design
blurb: Cognitive and learning science that design leans on.

cards.prompt: Define: working memory capacity (and why it matters for UI)
cards.answer: The small amount of information people can hold and manipulate at once, about 4 chunks (Cowan); interfaces should show options rather than make people remember them.

points.idea: hold and manipulate information at once

cards.answer: Recognizing something you see is easier than recalling it from memory, so interfaces should make options and information visible.
Learning is retained longer when study is spread out over time rather than crammed into one session.
Actively recalling information from memory strengthens it more than re-reading or re-studying it.
Information you produce yourself, like typing a definition, is remembered better than information you only read.
How well your confidence matches your actual performance; overconfidence means feeling you know more than you do.
The amount of mental effort working memory is using; good design removes unnecessary (extraneous) load so effort goes to the task.
Failing to notice a visible change, especially when it happens during a distraction or out of focus; why UI changes need feedback or motion cues.

points.idea: even when visible / during a disruption
